outline.description: This chapter establishes the context for the research, explaining the rise of large foundation models and the computational necessity of adapting them rather than training from scratch. It reviews existing fine-tuning paradigms and introduces the specific challenges associated with preserving pre-trained knowledge.
subtopics: The Era of Large Foundation Models: Scale and Cost
Three Paradigms of Adaptation: Full Fine-Tuning, Adapter Tuning, and Prompt Tuning
The Case for Model Fine-Tuning: Simplicity and Zero Inference Latency
Preserving Pre-trained Knowledge: The Role of Weight Similarity
Limitations of Ad-Hoc Approaches vs. Principled Constraints

outline.description: Here, we deep-dive into the foundational method upon which the paper builds: Orthogonal Fine-Tuning. We explain the mathematical motivation for using orthogonal transformations to preserve neuron angles, the implementation details, and the critical bottleneck regarding parameter efficiency that necessitates further innovation.
subtopics: Geometric Motivation: Preserving Pairwise Angles Between Neurons
Mathematical Formulation: Multiplicative Updates vs. Additive Low-Rank Updates (LoRA)
Ensuring Orthogonality: The Cayley Transform Parameterization
The Block-Diagonal Approximation: Trading Expressivity for Efficiency
Critical Analysis: Inductive Biases and Sparsity Patterns in Standard OFT

outline.chapter_title: A New Perspective: The Information Transmission Framework
outline.description: This chapter introduces the core theoretical contribution of the paper: reframing matrix factorization as an information transmission problem on a graph. This conceptual shift allows for a systematic design of sparse matrix products that can reconstruct dense connectivity efficiently.
subtopics: Conceptual Shift: Matrix Multiplication as Sequential Information Flow
Graph Representation: Grid-Structured Nodes and Directed Edges
Defining Desiderata: Dense Connectivity vs. Minimum Free Edges
Analyzing Sparsity Patterns through Graph Topology
Why Block-Diagonal Structures Fail to Achieve Global Density

outline.chapter_title: The Butterfly Structure and Efficient Parameterization
outline.description: Drawing inspiration from signal processing, this chapter details the adoption of the Cooley-Tukey butterfly structure. It explains how recursive sparse matrix factorization can generate dense orthogonal matrices with logarithmic parameter complexity, forming the backbone of the proposed BOFT method.
subtopics: Inspiration from Signal Processing: The Cooley-Tukey Fast Fourier Transform
Anatomy of a Butterfly Graph: Efficient Node Exchange
Mathematical Definition: Butterfly Factors and Recursive Construction
Constructing Orthogonal Butterfly Components via Block Permutations
Complexity Analysis: Reducing Parameters from O(d^2) to O(d log d)

outline.description: This chapter synthesizes the previous concepts into the complete BOFT algorithm. It covers the specific architecture of the method, initialization strategies to ensure stability at the start of training, and novel regularization techniques like Multiplicative Dropout designed specifically for multiplicative updates.
subtopics: The BOFT Architecture: Product of Sparse Orthogonal Matrices
_hyperparameters_: Understanding Depth (m) and Block Size (b)
_generalization_: How BOFT Subsumes Standard OFT as a Special Case
_initialization_strategy_: Identity Initialization for Stable Start Points
_regularization_technique_: Designing Multiplicative Dropout for Orthogonal Blocks
